content: 1. Procedures are established for communication with aircraft and air transport operators regarding free pratique (including radio free pratique) requests and authorizations, as well as the health section of the General Declaration of Aircraft, when requested by national authorities. 2. Procedures are in place for communication with ship and maritime industry operators concerning free pratique (including radio free pratique) requests and authorizations, and the Maritime Health Declaration, as required by national authorities. 3. Designated ship quarantine anchorage areas are arranged, based on risk assessments (e.g., vector-borne diseases, ballast water, waste, and other public health risks) and in accordance with safety, security, and facilitation principles. 4. Communication protocols with ground transport operators are established for border control measures when mass suspect cases or high public health risks are detected, as requested by national authorities. 5. Arrangements are in place to implement public health measures on affected ground transport vehicles, as recommended or requested by national authorities. 6. A Public Health Emergency Contingency Plan is established and maintained, including the nomination of a coordinator and contact points for relevant points of entry, public health, and other agencies and services. 7. The contingency plan is integrated with other public health response plans at national, intermediate, and local levels, as well as other emergency operational plans at points of entry, ensuring coordination among all relevant services. 8. Training and periodic drills are conducted to familiarize key personnel at points of entry with the public health contingency plan and their respective roles and responsibilities. 9. Arrangements are made with local medical and veterinary facilities for the isolation, treatment, and care of affected travelers or animals, including access to diagnostic tests, infection control measures, and necessary equipment. 10. Designated hygienic and environmentally safe spaces are provided for interviewing suspect or affected travelers, with independent exit passages to avoid cross-contamination. 11. Regularly updated and tested control measures, including cleaning, disinfection, and decontamination equipment, are in place to eliminate contamination risks at facilities used for interviewing affected travelers. 12. Procedures are established for the assessment and quarantine of suspect travelers, preferably in facilities away from the point of entry, with trained personnel available for timely interviews and first assessments. 13. Formal agreements with local hospitals, clinics, and health services are in place to receive suspected travelers for quarantine and other support services, with access to laboratory facilities and necessary equipment. 14. Measures are implemented to disinfect, derat, decontaminate, or otherwise treat conveyances, baggage, cargo, containers, goods, or postal parcels at specially designated and equipped locations. 15. Safe and hygienic transport arrangements are in place for transferring suspected travelers to medical or quarantine facilities, with trained personnel and appropriate protective equipment. 16. An Excel Spreadsheet File Model has been developed to summarize the results of assessments of core capacity requirements at designated airports, ports, and ground crossings, facilitating monitoring and planning for implementation. 17. The spreadsheet model generates numerical results, including percentages, to gauge gaps between current implementation status and International Health Regulations (IHR) core capacity requirements, supporting monitoring and follow-up actions.
